newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks end stronger on futures, telecoms.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks end stronger on futures, telecoms.

text.p: Brazil shares ended broadly higher in active trade on brisk futures dealings, a rally in telecom stocks, and optimism that stock transactions will be exempt from a new tax, brokers said.
"There was a lot of upward pressure today," said one dealer. "The exchange was also helped by a recovery in markets overseas as it appears the United States won't raise interest rates."
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 49 most-traded shares advanced 1.85 percent to close at 69,104 points on heavy volume of 727.3 million reais ($700.9 million).
Brokers said turnover was high because of the futures expiry today.

The market rose on busy futures trade combined with hope that stocks may be exempt from the CPMF tax and a rally in telecoms on Tuesday's sale of a strategic stake in Rio Grande do Sul state telecom CRT, they added.
"CRT was a good psychological factor for the market," one broker said. "It shows there are good prospects for telecoms."
The 35 percent stake in Cia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes (CRT) was bought by a Brazilian-Spanish group for 681 million reais, 54.8 percent over its base price.
The rise in telecoms was led by Telesp, the operating unit of federal giant Telebras for Sao Paulo state, but the session saw rises in most telephone company stocks.
Telesp preferred rose 5.77 percent to 220 reais, while bolsa benchmark Telebras preferred climbed 1.28 percent to close at 78.20 reais, and its common ended 1.24 percent higher 72.39 reais.
But the session also saw hikes, on smaller volumes, in some power sector stocks with bright prospects for privatization.

The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index of nine most liquid power shares surged 2.77 percent to close at 1,879 points. Sao Paulo state's CESP which jumped 13.06 percent to end at 40.70 reais and Minas Gerais state's Cemig jumped 3.98 percent to 34 reais.
Despite their rise, state power holding Eletrobras' preferred B share dipped 0.55 percent to end at 398 reais.
Leading bank Itau surged 13.86 percent to close at 459.99 reais on thin trade but the reason for the sharp rise was not immediately clear, brokers said.
